html:
Kl'bal Pom is one of the local divisions of the Wintu, a Wintuan-speaking people of the upper Sacramento River valley in northern California, here on the west side of the valley near today's Redding. Wintu territory was divided into bands named for their land, each with its own villages, fishing places and acorn groves.

They fished for salmon, gathered acorns and traded with the Shasta to the north. From the 1850s the Gold Rush brought miners, massacres and disease that killed most Wintu, and in the 1940s Shasta Dam flooded much of their land. See also Nom Ti Pom and Northern Wintu.
